title.es: Debate por el parque del barrio

es: Defender una postura en un debate vecinal integrando tesis, argumentos, concesión, refutación enfática y conclusión.

teaching.en: As a resident, I argue that the park should stay open until ten at night.
teaching.es: Como vecino, sostengo que el parque debería seguir abierto hasta las diez de la noche.
teaching.explanationEs: La tesis va al principio y dice claramente qué defiendes: I argue that…
segments: As a resident, I argue that the park
should stay open until ten at night.
teaching.audioText: As a resident, I argue that the park should stay open until ten at night.

teaching.en: Much as I respect the council, the petition shows that neighbours want longer hours.
teaching.es: Por mucho que respete al ayuntamiento, la petición muestra que los vecinos quieren un horario más largo.
teaching.explanationEs: Much as… concede y la frase siguiente da el argumento con su evidencia.
segments: Much as I respect the council, the
petition shows that neighbours want longer hours.
teaching.audioText: Much as I respect the council, the petition shows that neighbours want longer hours.

teaching.en: Admittedly, there is some rubbish after the weekend; nevertheless, the playground is used every evening.
teaching.es: Es cierto que hay algo de basura tras el fin de semana; sin embargo, la zona de juegos se usa cada tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Admittedly + nevertheless encadenan concesión y refutación en una sola frase.
segments: Admittedly, there is some rubbish after the weekend;
nevertheless, the playground is used every evening.
teaching.audioText: Admittedly, there is some rubbish after the weekend; nevertheless, the playground is used every evening.

teaching.en: What matters is that families have a safe place, and it is the council that must provide it.
teaching.es: Lo que importa es que las familias tengan un lugar seguro, y es el ayuntamiento quien debe ofrecerlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Dos frases hendidas seguidas: What matters is… y It is… that…
segments: What matters is that families have a safe place,
and it is the council that must provide it.
teaching.audioText: What matters is that families have a safe place, and it is the council that must provide it.

teaching.en: If the residents vote for the plan, the council can build a new playground.
teaching.es: Si los vecinos votan a favor del plan, el ayuntamiento puede construir una nueva zona de juegos.
teaching.explanationEs: Un argumento con consecuencia: if + presente, y luego can + verbo.
segments: If the residents vote for the plan,
the council can build a new playground.
teaching.audioText: If the residents vote for the plan, the council can build a new playground.

teaching.en: To conclude, a compromise is possible: longer hours with a cleaning team at weekends.
teaching.es: Para concluir, un acuerdo es posible: horario más largo con un equipo de limpieza los fines de semana.
teaching.explanationEs: El cierre propone un término medio y resume la postura en una frase.
segments: To conclude, a compromise is possible: longer
hours with a cleaning team at weekends.
teaching.audioText: To conclude, a compromise is possible: longer hours with a cleaning team at weekends.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mi postura es que el parque debe abrir hasta las diez.»

answer.text: My position is that the park should open until ten

feedback.es: La tesis se anuncia con My position is that… y después viene la propuesta completa.

hint.es: Empieza por My position is that y termina con until ten.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es cierto que hay basura; sin embargo, el parque se usa cada día.»

feedback.es: Nevertheless gira desde la concesión hacia la postura que se defiende.

hint.es: Es el conector que abre la refutación tras la concesión.

origin.text: Admittedly, there is rubbish; ___, the park is used every day.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que cierra bien una intervención en el debate.

choices.text: Admittedly, the park is busy at night.
To conclude, a compromise is possible: open until ten.
First, the survey shows that families need the park.

feedback.es: El cierre lleva una señal de conclusión y propone un término medio; las otras abren la concesión o el primer argumento.

hint.es: La frase de cierre lleva una señal que anuncia la conclusión.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué evidencia da la hablante a favor de la petición.

choices.text: The council has built a new playground.
Four hundred people have signed it.

feedback.es: La cifra de firmas es la evidencia; las quejas son lo que concede y la zona de juegos nueva no se menciona.

origin.audio: First, the petition has four hundred signatures. Second, the council has no other playground in this area. Admittedly, the noise complaints are fair; still, what matters is the children.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por muy fuerte que sea el ruido, los niños necesitan un sitio para jugar.»

feedback.es: However + adjetivo + sujeto + verbo forma la concesión; loud describe el ruido.

origin.text: However ___ the noise is, children need a place to play.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es una frase hendida que destaca lo esencial?

choices.text: What matters is that families feel safe.
Families feel safe in the park.
Families are safe, and the park is open.

feedback.es: What matters is… coloca en primer plano lo que se considera esencial.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención en el debate del parque, de tesis a conclusión.

answer.text: As a resident, my position is that the park should stay open until ten at night. First, the petition has four hundred signatures, which shows that many neighbours want longer hours. Second, there is no other playground in this area, so families have nowhere else to go after work. Admittedly, there is some noise and rubbish after the weekend, and I understand that the people who live next to the park are tired. Nevertheless, what matters is that children and parents have a safe place in the evening. It is the council that should clean the park and watch the noise, not the families who use it. Arguably, closing at eight would solve one problem and create a bigger one. To conclude, a compromise is possible: the park opens until ten, with a quiet rule after nine.
accepted: As a resident, my position is that the park should stay open until ten at night. First, the petition has four hundred signatures, which shows that many neighbours want longer hours. Second, there is no other playground in this area, so families have nowhere else to go after work. Admittedly, there is some noise and rubbish after the weekend, and I understand that the people who live next to the park are tired. Nevertheless, what matters is that children and parents have a safe place in the evening. It is the council that should clean the park and watch the noise, not the families who use it. Arguably, closing at eight would solve one problem and create a bigger one. To conclude, a compromise is possible: the park opens until ten, with a quiet rule after nine.

In my view, the park should remain open until ten at night. First, the petition has 400 signatures, so the residents clearly want longer hours. Second, there is no other playground nearby, and families need somewhere safe to go after work. Much as I understand the noise problem, what matters is that children and parents have a safe place in the evening. I concede that there is some rubbish at weekends; nevertheless, it is the council that must keep the park clean, not the families. Arguably, closing earlier would only move the problem somewhere else. To conclude, a compromise is possible: the park stays open until ten, with silence after nine.

feedback.es: Una intervención completa tiene tesis, dos argumentos con datos, concesión, refutación con frase hendida y cierre con acuerdo.

origin.text: Debate vecinal: ¿debe el parque abrir hasta las diez de la noche? Defiendes que sí. Incluye: tesis; dos argumentos (una petición con 400 firmas y que no hay otra zona de juegos); una concesión sobre el ruido y la basura; una refutación con frase hendida; y una conclusión con un acuerdo (silencio desde las nueve).

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué concede la hablante.

choices.text: That she supports a late opening.

feedback.es: La concesión va tras Admittedly; Even so abre su refutación sobre el sueño de los vecinos.

origin.audio: I cannot support a late opening. Admittedly, the playground is popular. Even so, the residents next to the park lose sleep.

prompt.es: Elige la reescritura de «Although the plan is expensive, we need it».

choices.text: Expensive as is the plan, we need it.
As expensive the plan is, we need it.
Expensive as the plan is, we need it.

feedback.es: El adjetivo abre la frase y le siguen as, el sujeto the plan y el verbo is, sin inversión.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es el ayuntamiento quien debe limpiar el parque.»

answer.text: It is the council that should clean the park

feedback.es: La frase hendida usa It is + the council + that para destacar al responsable.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pieza es la frase del ayuntamiento en el texto?

feedback.es: El ayuntamiento responde a la objeción de los vecinos, así que su frase es una réplica.

origin.text: Some residents object that the park will be too noisy. The council replies that new lights will make it safer.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por mucho que respete al ayuntamiento, la petición es justa.»

feedback.es: Much as + sujeto + verbo equivale a «por mucho que» y abre la concesión.

origin.text: ___ as I respect the council, the petition is fair.

prompt.es: Concede un punto y rebátelo con tacto.

answer.text: Admittedly, the park is noisy; nevertheless, children need a place to play.
accepted: Admittedly, the park is noisy; nevertheless, children need a place to play.
I concede that the park is noisy, but children need a place to play.
Admittedly, the park is loud, but children need somewhere to play.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta concede el ruido con Admittedly y rebate con nevertheless o but.

origin.text: Concede que el parque hace ruido y rebate que los niños necesitan jugar.
